scenario: Arguing a nuanced philosophical position
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Common for 'to argue' or 'to hold a view'.
Often used in plural 'matices'.
As a noun, not the adjective 'supposed'.
Frequently used in philosophical debate.
Introduces a condition, more formal than 'si'.
Used to contrast two ideas.
Often used to concede a point.
Followed by 'de'.
More formal than 'implicar'.
Core term in logical argumentation.
Connects conclusion to premises.
Introduces a concession.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yo sostengo que el libre albedrío es compatible con el determinismo, siempre que entendamos el determinismo con matices.
dialogue.translation: I maintain that free will is compatible with determinism, provided that we understand determinism with nuances.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ciertamente, pero tu postura carece de una distinción clara entre causas internas y externas.
dialogue.translation: Admittedly, but your position lacks a clear distinction between internal and external causes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No es que carezca de distinción; es que esa distinción no entraña una diferencia relevante para la responsabilidad moral.
dialogue.translation: It's not that it lacks a distinction; it's that that distinction does not entail a relevant difference for moral responsibility.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Pero entonces, ¿qué papel juegan los supuestos de tu argumento? Porque si aceptamos tus premisas, la conclusión parece inevitable.
dialogue.translation: But then, what role do the assumptions of your argument play? Because if we accept your premises, the conclusion seems inevitable.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mis supuestos son mínimos; en cambio, los tuyos implican una visión moral que no comparto.
dialogue.translation: My assumptions are minimal; on the other hand, yours imply a moral vision that I do not share.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aunque no compartas esa visión, no puedes ignorar que sin ella tu argumento carece de fuerza normativa.
dialogue.translation: Even though you don't share that vision, you cannot ignore that without it your argument lacks normative force.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Una objeción interesante, pero creo que confundes fuerza normativa con validez lógica.
dialogue.translation: An interesting objection, but I think you confuse normative force with logical validity.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quizá, pero por tanto tu posición no responde al problema real de la agencia moral.
dialogue.translation: Perhaps, but therefore your position does not respond to the real problem of moral agency.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Al contrario, es precisamente esa complejidad la que mi enfoque intenta captar, aunque sea imperfectamente.
dialogue.translation: On the contrary, it is precisely that complexity that my approach tries to capture, although imperfectly.

scenario: Discussing the limits of free speech
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often used in plural 'límites' to mean 'limits' or 'boundaries'.
Common in phrases like 'libertad de expresión' (freedom of speech).
Used in legal and social contexts; 'expresión' can be abstract.
Commonly used with 'que' + subjunctive.
Often used in the negative to discuss restrictions.
Can be literal or figurative.
Frequently used with 'contra' (against).
Often used in formal or academic settings.
Used with 'tener' or 'dar'.
Can also be a noun meaning 'audience'.
Often used in plural 'derechos'. Also means 'straight' or 'law'.
Used to express a condition or simultaneity.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: El debate sobre los límites de la libertad de expresión se ha vuelto muy tenso últimamente.
dialogue.translation: The debate about the limits of freedom of speech has become very tense lately.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero creo que hay que proteger el derecho a opinar, aunque a veces sea impopular.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but I think we have to protect the right to have an opinion, even if it's sometimes unpopular.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: De acuerdo, pero ¿qué pasa cuando esa opinión puede dañar a un grupo público?
dialogue.translation: Agreed, but what happens when that opinion can harm a public group?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ahí está el límite: no se debe permitir el discurso que incita a la violencia.
dialogue.translation: That's where the limit is: we should not allow speech that incites violence.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pero quien decide dónde está ese límite? A veces se prohíbe algo solo porque es ofensivo.
dialogue.translation: But who decides where that limit is? Sometimes something is prohibited just because it's offensive.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Es cierto, pero la ley existe para proteger a los vulnerables, mientras no se convierta en censura.
dialogue.translation: That's true, but the law exists to protect the vulnerable, as long as it doesn't become censorship.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entiendo, pero me preocupa que el debate se centre solo en lo prohibido y no en el diálogo.
dialogue.translation: I understand, but I'm worried that the debate focuses only on what's prohibited and not on dialogue.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Buen punto. Quizás deberíamos enfocarnos en promover un discurso respetuoso, sin necesidad de prohibir todo.
dialogue.translation: Good point. Maybe we should focus on promoting respectful discourse, without needing to prohibit everything.

key_phrases.phrase: límites de la libertad de expresión
mientras no se convierta en censura
key_phrases.translation: as long as it doesn't become censorship

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Puedes señalar algún ejemplo de parcialidad en este artículo?
dialogue.translation: Can you point out any example of bias in this article?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro, el enfoque claramente favorece a una parte; omiten datos clave.
dialogue.translation: Sure, the approach clearly favors one side; they omit key data.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Es evidente que el autor apoya una postura, pero en cambio no menciona la otra.
dialogue.translation: It's evident that the author supports one stance, whereas they don't mention the other.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, y las fuentes que cita son casi todas de la misma organización.
dialogue.translation: Yes, and the sources they cite are almost all from the same organization.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Crees que el criterio editorial es deficiente o que lo hicieron a propósito?
dialogue.translation: Do you think the editorial judgment is deficient or that they did it on purpose?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quizás no lo hicieron a propósito, pero deberían rechazar ese tipo de prácticas.
dialogue.translation: Perhaps they didn't do it on purpose, but they should reject that kind of practice.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Justamente, un periodista debe ser consciente de sus propios sesgos.
dialogue.translation: Precisely, a journalist must be aware of their own biases.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Totalmente, y también hay que analizar qué información se omite deliberadamente.
dialogue.translation: Absolutely, and we also need to analyze what information is deliberately omitted.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: En resumen, es crucial evaluar el enfoque, las fuentes y el criterio para detectar parcialidad.
dialogue.translation: In summary, it's crucial to evaluate the approach, sources, and judgment to detect bias.

scenario: Debating economic inequality and systemic causes
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

Core term for this topic.

Used with wealth, capital, etc.

Transitive: 'beneficiar a alguien'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: La brecha entre ricos y pobres sigue ampliándose, pese a los discursos sobre movilidad social.
dialogue.translation: The gap between rich and poor keeps widening, despite the rhetoric about social mobility.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero la desigualdad no es solo un accidente; se debe a que el sistema beneficia a los ya privilegiados.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but inequality is not just an accident; it's because the system benefits those already privileged.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y cómo se acumula tanta riqueza en tan pocas manos? No me parece justo, desde luego.
dialogue.translation: And how is so much wealth accumulated in so few hands? It doesn't seem fair to me, certainly.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Se logra mediante mecanismos fiscales que excluyen a la mayoría, y además la educación de calidad es escasa para muchos.
dialogue.translation: It's achieved through fiscal mechanisms that exclude the majority, and furthermore, quality education is scarce for many.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¿propondrías redistribuir la riqueza de forma forzosa? Eso me parece injusto para quien ha trabajado.
dialogue.translation: So, would you propose forcibly redistributing wealth? That seems unfair to someone who has worked.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No digo confiscar, pero un sistema que no corrige la brecha inicial perpetúa el privilegio, y eso también es injusto.
dialogue.translation: I'm not saying confiscate, but a system that doesn't correct the initial gap perpetuates privilege, and that is also unfair.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quizás el problema no sea la riqueza en sí, sino que algunos quedan excluidos de las oportunidades básicas.
dialogue.translation: Maybe the problem isn't wealth itself, but that some are excluded from basic opportunities.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exacto, y pese a los avances técnicos, la movilidad social sigue siendo un mito para muchos, porque los recursos son escasos y mal distribuidos.
dialogue.translation: Exactly, and despite technical advances, social mobility remains a myth for many, because resources are scarce and poorly distributed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: En fin, es un debate complejo; pero al menos coincidimos en que la desigualdad no es inevitable.
dialogue.translation: Anyway, it's a complex debate; but at least we agree that inequality is not inevitable.

key_phrases.phrase: la brecha entre ricos y pobres
key_phrases.translation: the gap between rich and poor

scenario: Discussing the ethics of genetic engineering
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Commonly used in academic and technical contexts.
Used to introduce a concession.
Often used metaphorically.
Frequent in argumentative discourse.

vocabulary.translation: in the face of, compared to
vocabulary.note: Used to contrast or position against.
Often used in formal or legal contexts.
Derived from 'prever'.
Can have negative connotations.
Common in social and scientific discussions.
Often used with 'correr' or 'asumir'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Crees que deberíamos permitir la modificación genética en la población general?
dialogue.translation: Do you think we should allow genetic modification in the general population?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Es un tema complejo, aunque creo que los riesgos son demasiado altos para aplicarla sin restricciones.
dialogue.translation: It's a complex issue, although I think the risks are too high to apply it without restrictions.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pero si podemos eliminar enfermedades hereditarias, ¿no sería beneficioso para todos?
dialogue.translation: But if we can eliminate hereditary diseases, wouldn't it be beneficial for everyone?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: El efecto inmediato puede ser positivo, pero las consecuencias a largo plazo son imprevisibles.
dialogue.translation: The immediate effect may be positive, but the long-term consequences are unpredictable.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sin embargo, con una regulación estricta podríamos garantizar que solo se use para fines médicos.
dialogue.translation: However, with strict regulation we could guarantee that it is only used for medical purposes.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: La duda es quién controla esa regulación y qué intereses hay detrás, frente a la ética.
dialogue.translation: The doubt is who controls that regulation and what interests are behind it, compared to ethics.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entiendo tu preocupación, pero no podemos dejar de avanzar por miedo a lo desconocido.
dialogue.translation: I understand your concern, but we cannot stop advancing for fear of the unknown.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No se trata de frenar el avance, sino de no manipular la naturaleza sin una base ética sólida.
dialogue.translation: It's not about stopping progress, but about not manipulating nature without a solid ethical basis.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Supongo que tienes razón: debemos equilibrar el potencial para aumentar la calidad de vida con la prudencia.
dialogue.translation: I suppose you're right: we must balance the potential to increase the quality of life with prudence.

key_phrases.translation: compared to ethics / in the face of ethics

scenario: Exploring the tension between tradition and innovation
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often used in contexts of maintaining traditions or heritage.
Abstract noun, frequently paired with 'tradición' in debates.
Past participle used as adjective; describes what we receive from the past.
Reflexive; often used with 'a' (adaptarse a).
Can refer to physical or metaphorical resistance to change.
Used to contrast two ideas.
Used for abstract concepts like innovation or education.
Frequency adverb, equivalent to 'frequently'.
Emotional or conceptual connection.
Formal synonym of 'duradero'.
Common in business and cultural contexts.
Formal connector, equivalent to 'therefore'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Creo que debemos preservar nuestras tradiciones, pero también incorporar nuevas ideas para no quedarnos atrás.
dialogue.translation: I think we must preserve our traditions, but also incorporate new ideas so we don't fall behind.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Estoy de acuerdo, aunque a menudo la resistencia al cambio viene de quienes temen perder su identidad.
dialogue.translation: I agree, although often resistance to change comes from those who fear losing their identity.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pero fomentar la innovación no significa destruir el legado heredado, sino adaptarse a los nuevos tiempos.
dialogue.translation: But promoting innovation doesn't mean destroying the inherited legacy, but rather adapting to new times.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Mientras que en las ciudades la modernidad avanza rápido, en el ámbito rural aún se valora más lo perdurable.
dialogue.translation: Whereas in cities modernity advances quickly, in rural areas what is lasting is still valued more.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ese vínculo con la tierra y la historia es esencial, pero no debería impedir la evolución.
dialogue.translation: That bond with the land and history is essential, but it shouldn't impede evolution.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exacto, y por consiguiente, necesitamos un equilibrio que permita renovar sin perder la esencia.
dialogue.translation: Exactly, and consequently, we need a balance that allows us to renew without losing the essence.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quizás la clave esté en valorar lo antiguo y, a la vez, abrirnos a lo nuevo de forma gradual.
dialogue.translation: Perhaps the key lies in valuing the old and, at the same time, opening ourselves to the new gradually.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sin duda, así lograremos una innovación que no rompa con el pasado, sino que lo enriquezca.
dialogue.translation: Undoubtedly, that way we will achieve an innovation that doesn't break with the past, but rather enriches it.

key_phrases.translation: to open oneself to the new

scenario: Analyzing a historical turning point
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often used for significant historical events

Used metaphorically to mean 'to propel forward'
Commonly used for major changes in society or systems

Emphasizes a clear cause-effect link

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Crees que la caída del muro de Berlín fue un acontecimiento que realmente impulsó la transformación de Europa?
dialogue.translation: Do you think the fall of the Berlin Wall was an event that really drove the transformation of Europe?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero no fue meramente un cambio político; provocó una conmoción social enorme que se sintió durante décadas.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but it was not merely a political change; it caused an enormous social upheaval that was felt for decades.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y no crees que a largo plazo las consecuencias fueron más complejas de lo que se anticipó?
dialogue.translation: And don't you think that in the long term the consequences were more complex than anticipated?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exacto, nadie previó que desencadenaría una serie de conflictos étnicos, aunque también abrió nuevas perspectivas de cooperación.
dialogue.translation: Exactly, no one foresaw that it would trigger a series of ethnic conflicts, although it also opened new perspectives for cooperation.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No obstante, muchos analistas subestiman el papel de la presión económica en ese proceso.
dialogue.translation: Nevertheless, many analysts underestimate the role of economic pressure in that process.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Cierto, pero la unificación alemana fue una consecuencia directa de ese cambio de equilibrio.
dialogue.translation: True, but German unification was a direct consequence of that shift in balance.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¿dirías que la transformación fue más profunda por la conmoción cultural que por lo político?
dialogue.translation: So, would you say that the transformation was deeper because of the cultural shock than because of the political?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sin duda, y a largo plazo eso ha tenido un efecto enorme en la identidad europea.
dialogue.translation: Without a doubt, and in the long term that has had an enormous effect on European identity.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Para mí, lo más importante es no subestimar cómo ese acontecimiento sigue impulsando debates actuales.
dialogue.translation: For me, the most important thing is not to underestimate how that event continues to drive current debates.

scenario: Discussing the nature of consciousness
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Used here in the sense of 'case' as an instance or example.
Often used in abstract contexts like ideas or phenomena.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Crees que la conciencia es un mero producto del cerebro, o acaso surge de algo más profundo?
dialogue.translation: Do you think consciousness is a mere product of the brain, or perhaps it arises from something deeper?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: En mi caso, tiendo a pensar que no es solo un fenómeno físico; semejante idea me parece demasiado reduccionista.
dialogue.translation: In my case, I tend to think it's not just a physical phenomenon; such an idea seems too reductionist to me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pero, ¿cómo podemos percibir algo que no se puede medir? Si la conciencia no es física, ¿cómo interactúa con el entorno?
dialogue.translation: But how can we perceive something that cannot be measured? If consciousness is not physical, how does it interact with the environment?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quizá la pregunta no sea cómo medirla, sino cómo abarcar todas sus dimensiones. La experiencia subjetiva es vasta y compleja.
dialogue.translation: Perhaps the question is not how to measure it, but how to encompass all its dimensions. Subjective experience is vast and complex.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¿propones que deberíamos indagar en ella desde una perspectiva filosófica, sin depender solo de la ciencia?
dialogue.translation: So, are you proposing that we should investigate it from a philosophical perspective, without relying only on science?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exacto. Sin embargo, no niego el valor de la neurociencia; simplemente creo que necesitamos un enfoque más integral.
dialogue.translation: Exactly. However, I don't deny the value of neuroscience; I simply think we need a more integrative approach.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y no te parece que semejante postura podría caer en el misticismo? A veces lo desconocido nos lleva a conclusiones poco rigurosas.
dialogue.translation: And don't you think such a stance could fall into mysticism? Sometimes the unknown leads us to conclusions that lack rigor.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Puede ser, pero acaso el misterio de la conciencia requiera precisamente esa apertura. Al final, es un vasto campo de estudio.
dialogue.translation: Maybe, but perhaps the mystery of consciousness requires precisely that openness. In the end, it is a vast field of study.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tienes un punto. Tal vez debamos aceptar que, por ahora, no podemos abarcar completamente este fenómeno. Sin embargo, es fascinante debatirlo.
dialogue.translation: You have a point. Perhaps we must accept that, for now, we cannot fully encompass this phenomenon. However, it is fascinating to debate it.

scenario: Debating criminal justice reform

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Creo que el sistema actual se enfoca demasiado en el castigo y no en la rehabilitación del delincuente.
dialogue.translation: I think the current system focuses too much on punishment and not on the rehabilitation of the offender.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Pero sin una pena proporcional, ¿cómo vamos a disuadir a otros de cometer un delito?
dialogue.translation: But without a proportionate sentence, how are we going to deter others from committing a crime?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: La disuasión no funciona si la gente ve que el sistema es injusto. Además, la reincidencia baja cuando hay programas de reinserción.
dialogue.translation: Deterrence doesn't work if people see the system as unfair. Moreover, recidivism drops when there are reintegration programs.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entiendo, pero hay delitos muy graves que merecen un castigo ejemplar. No todo se resuelve con terapia.
dialogue.translation: I understand, but there are very serious crimes that deserve exemplary punishment. Not everything is solved with therapy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nadie dice que no haya que juzgar a los culpables, pero la condena debería buscar la reinserción, no solo el castigo.
dialogue.translation: Nobody says we shouldn't judge the guilty, but the sentence should seek reintegration, not just punishment.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: De acuerdo, pero ¿qué hacemos con los que reinciden una y otra vez? Ahí la prueba de que el sistema no funciona es clara.
dialogue.translation: Agreed, but what do we do with those who reoffend again and again? There the proof that the system doesn't work is clear.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Precisamente, la reincidencia es alta porque las cárceles no rehabilitan. Deberíamos invertir en educación y apoyo laboral.
dialogue.translation: Precisely, recidivism is high because prisons don't rehabilitate. We should invest in education and job support.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Y también en procesos más justos para no enjuiciar a inocentes. Pero el indulto no puede ser un mecanismo para vaciar las cárceles.
dialogue.translation: And also in fairer processes so as not to prosecute innocents. But pardon cannot be a mechanism to empty prisons.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Claro, el indulto debe ser excepcional. Lo que necesitamos es una reforma integral que equilibre castigo y reinserción.
dialogue.translation: Of course, pardon should be exceptional. What we need is a comprehensive reform that balances punishment and reintegration.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hasta cierto punto, pero también creo que los hablantes pueden superar esas limitaciones con esfuerzo y creatividad.
dialogue.translation: To some extent, but I also believe that speakers can overcome those limitations with effort and creativity.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¿dirías que el idioma no determina el pensamiento, sino que lo moldea parcialmente?
dialogue.translation: Then, would you say that language does not determine thought, but rather shapes it partially?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, y además cada idioma ofrece recursos únicos para expresar matices que en otros requieren rodeos.
dialogue.translation: Yes, and furthermore each language offers unique resources to express nuances that in others require circumlocution.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Me parece fascinante cómo el vocabulario de un idioma puede reflejar las prioridades de una cultura.
dialogue.translation: I find it fascinating how a language's vocabulary can reflect the priorities of a culture.

scenario: Discussing the role of art in political resistance
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Used for ideas, movements, or situations that appear.
Commonly refers to a public protest, but also means 'manifestation' in a broader sense.
Refers to the suppression of speech or art.
Used to publicly condemn or expose wrongdoing.
Often used in political contexts to describe suppression of dissent.
Describes something that aims to undermine authority or systems.
A person who opposes official policy, or the adjective describing such opposition.
Used to describe art that deeply affects people emotionally.
Used metaphorically to mean a means of expression or opinion.
As adjective: collective; as noun: a group or collective (e.g., artist collective).
Used with 'a' when confronting something/someone.
Used to express contrast; followed by a noun or infinitive.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Crees que el arte realmente puede tener un impacto político o es solo una forma de expresión?
dialogue.translation: Do you think art really can have a political impact or is it just a form of expression?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sin duda. En muchos países, el arte ha sido una herramienta para denunciar la represión y dar voz a los que no la tienen.
dialogue.translation: Absolutely. In many countries, art has been a tool to denounce repression and give a voice to those who don't have one.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pero a veces la censura es tan fuerte que los artistas tienen que enfrentarse a consecuencias graves, ¿no?
dialogue.translation: But sometimes censorship is so strong that artists have to face serious consequences, right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exacto. A pesar de los riesgos, muchos artistas disidentes continúan creando obras subversivas que conmueven a la sociedad.
dialogue.translation: Exactly. Despite the risks, many dissident artists continue creating subversive works that move society.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Es interesante cómo una manifestación artística puede surgir de la nada y convertirse en un símbolo de lucha colectiva.
dialogue.translation: It's interesting how an artistic manifestation can arise from nothing and become a symbol of collective struggle.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, y eso es precisamente lo que los gobiernos autoritarios temen: que el arte despierte una conciencia crítica en la gente.
dialogue.translation: Yes, and that is precisely what authoritarian governments fear: that art awakens a critical conscience in people.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¿crees que el arte es más efectivo que la protesta callejera?
dialogue.translation: So, do you think art is more effective than street protest?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No diría más efectivo, sino complementario. La protesta moviliza, pero el arte perdura en la memoria y puede transformar la percepción a largo plazo.
dialogue.translation: I wouldn't say more effective, but rather complementary. Protest mobilizes, but art endures in memory and can transform perception in the long term.

scenario: Analyzing the paradoxes of globalization
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Commonly used for quantities, intensity, or degree.
Opposite of aumentar; used for size, amount, or scope.
Can be economic or social; often plural 'beneficios'.
Frequently used in social/economic contexts.
Related to the whole world; not 'mundial' (more common) but still frequent.
Opposite of global; often used in contrast.
Can be literal (national borders) or figurative.
Used for movement of goods, people, information.
Often followed by 'de'.
More formal than 'a pesar de' but synonymous.
Used to introduce a contrasting idea; similar to 'sin embargo'.
Used to emphasize a statement.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Lo curioso es que la globalización debería reducir las desigualdades, pero ciertamente las ha aumentado en muchos países.
dialogue.translation: The curious thing is that globalization should reduce inequalities, but it has certainly increased them in many countries.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exacto, y no obstante, el flujo de información global permite que las comunidades locales se organicen mejor que antes.
dialogue.translation: Exactly, and nevertheless, the global flow of information allows local communities to organize better than before.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pero ese flujo también depende de las grandes corporaciones, cuyo único beneficio parece ser económico, no social.
dialogue.translation: But that flow also depends on large corporations, whose only benefit seems to be economic, not social.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Cierto, pese a la retórica de aldea global, las fronteras siguen siendo barreras duras para millones de migrantes.
dialogue.translation: True, despite the rhetoric of a global village, borders remain hard barriers for millions of migrants.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Y mientras tanto, las decisiones en un país afectan a otro sin que haya una autoridad global que regule ese impacto.
dialogue.translation: And meanwhile, decisions in one country affect another without there being a global authority that regulates that impact.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No obstante, también hay ejemplos positivos: la cooperación científica global ha reducido el tiempo para desarrollar vacunas.
dialogue.translation: Nevertheless, there are also positive examples: global scientific cooperation has reduced the time to develop vaccines.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pero esa cooperación no siempre llega a las zonas rurales; el beneficio se concentra en las ciudades, aumentando la brecha local.
dialogue.translation: But that cooperation does not always reach rural areas; the benefit is concentrated in cities, increasing the local gap.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: En resumen, la globalización es un fenómeno lleno de paradojas: ciertamente no es ni totalmente buena ni totalmente mala.
dialogue.translation: In short, globalization is a phenomenon full of paradoxes: it is certainly neither totally good nor totally bad.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: De acuerdo, y tal vez el verdadero desafío sea gestionar sus efectos para que no dependamos tanto de los intereses de unos pocos.
dialogue.translation: Agreed, and perhaps the real challenge is to manage its effects so that we don't depend so much on the interests of a few.

scenario: Exploring concepts of identity and belonging
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Core concept; often used with 'cultural' or 'nacional'.
Usually in phrases like 'sentido de pertenencia'.
Emotional or social connection.
Often plural 'raíces' for cultural roots.
Used for upbringing, not for objects.
Can be literal (property) or figurative (traits).
Commonly used for cultures or identities.
Often with 'a': 'ajeno a' = unrelated to.
Used to emphasize ownership or typical feature.
Reflexive; often with 'parte de' or 'identificado con'.
Introduces contrast.
Formal; followed by a noun or infinitive.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Inevitablemente, mi identidad se ha formado mediante una mezcla de culturas, aunque a veces me siento ajeno a ambas.
dialogue.translation: Inevitably, my identity has been formed through a mix of cultures, although sometimes I feel alien to both.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero ¿qué te da un sentido de pertenencia? ¿Tienes algún vínculo fuerte con un lugar o con una comunidad?
dialogue.translation: Yes, but what gives you a sense of belonging? Do you have any strong bond with a place or a community?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Creo que mis raíces son importantes, aunque no crecí allí. Mi familia me crió con historias de nuestro país de origen.
dialogue.translation: I think my roots are important, although I didn't grow up there. My family raised me with stories from our country of origin.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Y has heredado esas tradiciones o las has adaptado a tu entorno actual?
dialogue.translation: And have you inherited those traditions or have you adapted them to your current environment?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: He intentado mantener lo propio, pero al vivir aquí, inevitablemente se mezclan las costumbres.
dialogue.translation: I've tried to keep what is my own, but living here, the customs inevitably blend.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: A veces me siento parte de varios mundos a la vez, pero nunca por completo de uno solo.
dialogue.translation: Sometimes I feel part of several worlds at once, but never completely of just one.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exacto. Y aunque no encaje del todo, he aprendido a valorar esa mezcla como algo enriquecedor.
dialogue.translation: Exactly. And although I don't fully fit in, I've learned to value that mix as something enriching.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¿dirías que tu identidad es más bien un híbrido, no algo ajeno a ti?
dialogue.translation: So, would you say your identity is rather a hybrid, not something alien to you?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, y mediante ese proceso he descubierto que el sentido de pertenencia no siempre depende de un lugar físico, sino de los vínculos que creamos.
dialogue.translation: Yes, and through that process I've discovered that the sense of belonging does not always depend on a physical place, but on the bonds we create.

scenario: Discussing the philosophy of work and purpose
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often used in phrases like 'sentido de la vida' (meaning of life).
Used in 'pleno sentido' (full sense) or 'plena realización' (full fulfillment).

vocabulary.translation: to fulfill oneself, to be realized

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Para mí, el trabajo no tiene sentido si solo se trata de subsistir; necesito que me aporte algo más.
dialogue.translation: For me, work has no meaning if it's only about surviving; I need it to contribute something more to me.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entiendo, pero ¿no crees que el logro profesional puede venir precisamente del esfuerzo diario, aunque sea meramente económico?
dialogue.translation: I understand, but don't you think professional achievement can come precisely from daily effort, even if it's merely economic?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sin embargo, el esfuerzo sin un propósito más amplio me parece vacío; es como un mero trámite para pagar facturas.
dialogue.translation: However, effort without a broader purpose seems empty to me; it's like a mere formality to pay bills.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Y no puede ser que el propósito se descubra frecuentemente a través del propio trabajo, no antes?
dialogue.translation: And couldn't it be that purpose is frequently discovered through the work itself, not before?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Puede ser, pero para realizarse plenamente, creo que necesitas una conexión entre lo que haces y lo que eres.
dialogue.translation: Maybe, but to fulfill yourself fully, I think you need a connection between what you do and what you are.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: De acuerdo, pero no todos tienen el privilegio de elegir; muchos trabajan solo para subsistir, y eso también es digno.
dialogue.translation: Agreed, but not everyone has the privilege to choose; many work just to survive, and that's also worthy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Claro, no quiero menospreciar eso, pero la cuestión es si el trabajo puede ser un medio para algo más, no un fin en sí mismo.
dialogue.translation: Of course, I don't want to belittle that, but the question is whether work can be a means to something more, not an end in itself.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Y mediante ese medio, quizás encontramos un sentido que no buscábamos; sin embargo, no siempre es así.
dialogue.translation: And through that means, perhaps we find a meaning we weren't looking for; however, that's not always the case.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Cierto, pero al final, la plena realización personal me parece un ideal más que una meta alcanzable para la mayoría.
dialogue.translation: True, but in the end, full personal fulfillment seems to me more of an ideal than an attainable goal for most.

scenario: Debating privacy vs security in the digital age
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Commonly used in plural 'datos' for 'data'.
Frequent in security contexts.
Though thematic, it's common in general discourse.
High-frequency, used in many contexts.
Often used in abstract and concrete senses.
Common in discussions of trade-offs.
Frequently used with 'a' (access to something).
Often used in contexts of information.
Core verb in security discussions.
Often used in plural 'derechos'.
Used to emphasize limitations or conditions.
Frequently used metaphorically (e.g., invasion of privacy).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No entiendo por qué tanta gente se opone a que el gobierno vigile nuestras comunicaciones.
dialogue.translation: I don't understand why so many people oppose the government monitoring our communications.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Porque eso supone una invasión de nuestra privacidad, un derecho que no deberíamos ceder tan fácilmente.
dialogue.translation: Because that involves an invasion of our privacy, a right we shouldn't give up so easily.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pero sin acceso a esos datos, no podemos detectar amenazas a tiempo. La seguridad también es un derecho.
dialogue.translation: But without access to that data, we can't detect threats in time. Security is also a right.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: De acuerdo, pero ¿hasta dónde llegamos? Si revelamos todo, perdemos por completo nuestra intimidad.
dialogue.translation: Agreed, but how far do we go? If we reveal everything, we completely lose our intimacy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No se trata de revelarlo todo, sino de equilibrar. Podemos proteger la seguridad sin violar todos los derechos.
dialogue.translation: It's not about revealing everything, but about balancing. We can protect security without violating all rights.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: El problema es que el acceso a nuestros datos no se limita estrictamente a casos de terrorismo; a veces se usa para otros fines.
dialogue.translation: The problem is that access to our data is not strictly limited to terrorism cases; sometimes it's used for other purposes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Cierto, pero ante una amenaza real, la urgencia justifica ciertas medidas excepcionales.
dialogue.translation: True, but in the face of a real threat, urgency justifies certain exceptional measures.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aun así, creo que debemos ser cautelosos. La vigilancia masiva puede convertirse en una herramienta de control social.
dialogue.translation: Even so, I think we must be cautious. Mass surveillance can become a tool of social control.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Es un debate complejo. Quizás la clave esté en encontrar un punto medio que nos permita vivir con seguridad sin sacrificar nuestra privacidad.
dialogue.translation: It's a complex debate. Maybe the key is to find a middle ground that allows us to live with security without sacrificing our privacy.

scenario: Exploring cultural imperialism and soft power
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often used in contexts of power dynamics.
Commonly used with 'cultura' or 'ideas'.
Can refer to a societal or cultural model.
Frequently appears in discussions of cultural products.
How something is viewed or understood.
Used for spreading ideas, culture, etc.
Often associated with soft power.
In context, adopting cultural practices or norms.
Opposition to external cultural influence.
Used to describe dominance of one culture over others.
Often used in 'intercambio mutuo' (mutual exchange).
Used to describe awareness of cultural influence.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Crees que la influencia de Estados Unidos en nuestra cultura es algo consciente o simplemente ocurre por el consumo de sus productos?
dialogue.translation: Do you think the influence of the United States on our culture is something conscious or simply happens through the consumption of their products?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Creo que es una mezcla, pero hay una intención clara de imponer su modelo económico y cultural a través del cine y la música.
dialogue.translation: I think it's a mix, but there's a clear intention to impose their economic and cultural model through film and music.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sin embargo, también hay una percepción positiva de lo estadounidense, ¿no? Eso les da prestigio y facilita que otros países adopten sus costumbres.
dialogue.translation: However, there's also a positive perception of American things, right? That gives them prestige and makes it easier for other countries to adopt their customs.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro, pero esa percepción no es natural; se construye a través de los medios que difunden sus valores constantemente.
dialogue.translation: Sure, but that perception isn't natural; it's built through the media that constantly spread their values.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¿qué papel juega la resistencia local frente a esa presión? ¿Puede predominar una cultura alternativa?
dialogue.translation: So, what role does local resistance play against that pressure? Can an alternative culture predominate?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: En algunos países hay una resistencia fuerte, pero a menudo se ve limitada porque el intercambio no es mutuo: ellos importan mucho, pero nosotros exportamos poco.
dialogue.translation: In some countries there's strong resistance, but it's often limited because the exchange isn't mutual: they import a lot, but we export little.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Y en ese intercambio desigual, ¿no perdemos algo de nuestra identidad? A veces ni siquiera somos conscientes de hasta qué punto adoptamos lo ajeno.
dialogue.translation: And in that unequal exchange, don't we lose some of our identity? Sometimes we aren't even aware of how much we adopt what's foreign.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exacto, y por eso es importante analizar críticamente qué consumimos y qué difundimos nosotros mismos, en lugar de seguir un modelo impuesto.
dialogue.translation: Exactly, and that's why it's important to critically analyze what we consume and what we spread ourselves, instead of following an imposed model.

scenario: Discussing the limits of scientific knowledge
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Common in academic discussions to mean taking something for granted.
General term for knowledge or understanding.
Refers to lack of certainty, often in scientific contexts.
Used for boundaries or limits, both physical and conceptual.
Refers to a systematic procedure, like the scientific method.
Key verb in science; to watch or notice carefully.
To forecast or say what will happen in the future.
In science, to demonstrate or verify a hypothesis.
A well-substantiated explanation, not just a guess.
To check or confirm the accuracy of something.
A close but not exact estimate or representation.
To challenge or doubt the validity of something.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Hasta qué punto podemos asumir que el conocimiento científico es objetivo?
dialogue.translation: To what extent can we assume that scientific knowledge is objective?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Pues, en teoría debería serlo, pero siempre hay un margen de incertidumbre debido a la aproximación de los modelos.
dialogue.translation: Well, in theory it should be, but there is always a margin of uncertainty due to the approximation of models.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exacto, y además el método científico tiene sus límites; no podemos observar todo directamente.
dialogue.translation: Exactly, and besides, the scientific method has its limits; we cannot observe everything directly.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro, por eso a veces es difícil predecir fenómenos complejos como el clima.
dialogue.translation: Of course, that's why it is sometimes difficult to predict complex phenomena like the climate.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Y aunque no podamos probar ciertas hipótesis, eso no significa que debamos cuestionar todo el avance científico.
dialogue.translation: And even if we cannot prove certain hypotheses, that does not mean we should question all scientific progress.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: De acuerdo, pero también es esencial verificar los resultados para evitar errores.
dialogue.translation: Agreed, but it is also essential to verify results to avoid mistakes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y crees que algún día superaremos esos límites?
dialogue.translation: And do you think we will ever overcome those limits?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quizás no del todo, porque la incertidumbre es inherente al proceso de conocer.
dialogue.translation: Perhaps not entirely, because uncertainty is inherent to the process of knowing.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¿debemos conformarnos con una aproximación a la verdad?
dialogue.translation: So, must we settle for an approximation to the truth?

scenario: Analyzing rhetoric and persuasion techniques
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Refers to a logical reason or set of reasons.
Regular -ir verb; often used with 'a alguien de algo'.
Can mean the people who listen/watch or an official hearing.
Refers to the art of persuasive speaking/writing.
Often used in media analysis: 'sesgo político'.
Can mean to handle skillfully or to influence unfairly.

vocabulary.translation: to evoke, to call to mind
vocabulary.note: Used for emotions or memories.
Common in analysis of rhetoric: 'una diferencia sutil'.
Derived from 'persuadir'.
Opposite of 'explícito'.
Often 'apelar a' (appeal to).
Used to describe subtle distinctions.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: El discurso del candidato me pareció muy persuasivo, pero noté un sesgo evidente en la selección de datos.
dialogue.translation: The candidate's speech seemed very persuasive to me, but I noticed an evident bias in the selection of data.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, apelaba constantemente a las emociones del público, pero no ofrecía un argumento sólido.
dialogue.translation: Yes, he constantly appealed to the emotions of the audience, but he didn't offer a solid argument.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exacto. La retórica era efectiva para persuadir a la audiencia, pero el contenido carecía de matices.
dialogue.translation: Exactly. The rhetoric was effective in persuading the audience, but the content lacked nuance.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Además, utilizaba palabras que evocan esperanza y miedo de manera casi sutil, sin ser demasiado explícito.
dialogue.translation: Moreover, he used words that evoke hope and fear in a subtle way, without being too explicit.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Crees que manipulaba la información o simplemente omitía lo que no le convenía?
dialogue.translation: Do you think he manipulated information or simply omitted what didn't suit him?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: En mi opinión, había un mensaje implícito que favorecía a ciertos grupos, aunque nunca lo dijo abiertamente.
dialogue.translation: In my opinion, there was an implicit message that favored certain groups, although he never said it openly.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Esa es la clave: lo que no se dice también persuade, porque el público tiende a completar las ideas por sí mismo.
dialogue.translation: That's the key: what is not said also persuades, because the audience tends to fill in the ideas themselves.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Precisamente. Un buen orador conoce a su audiencia y adapta su discurso para lograr ese efecto, sin parecer manipulador.
dialogue.translation: Precisely. A good speaker knows his audience and adapts his speech to achieve that effect, without seeming manipulative.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Y para analizarlo bien, hay que separar la emoción del razonamiento y buscar el matiz que revela la verdadera intención.
dialogue.translation: And to analyze it well, you have to separate emotion from reasoning and look for the nuance that reveals the true intention.

scenario: Exploring the ethics of humanitarian intervention
frequency_note: words ranked ~3000–6000 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Common in formal discussions to mean 'to deal with a topic'.
Often used with 'tener' (to have consequences) or 'como consecuencia' (as a result).
In plural 'criterios' means 'criteria'; also 'criterio' can mean 'good sense'.
Frequently used in ethical debates: 'justificar una acción'.
Opposite: 'ilegítimo'. Often used with 'gobierno' or 'acción'.
Common in contexts of conflicts and international relations.
Used when deliberately not mentioning something.
Distinguish from 'prever' (to foresee). 'Prevenir' implies taking action.
Often in plural 'recursos' (resources, financial means).
More formal than 'apoyar'; used in political/institutional contexts.
Intransitive; often used with 'problema', 'duda', 'conflicto'.
In phrases like 'buena voluntad' (goodwill) or 'voluntad política' (political will).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Para abordar el tema de la intervención humanitaria, primero debemos definir con claridad cuándo es legítimo actuar sin el consentimiento del Estado.
dialogue.translation: To address the issue of humanitarian intervention, we must first clearly define when it is legitimate to act without the consent of the state.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: De acuerdo, pero no podemos omitir el principio de neutralidad: si ayudamos a una de las partes, ¿no perdemos nuestra imparcialidad?
dialogue.translation: Agreed, but we cannot omit the principle of neutrality: if we help one of the parties, don't we lose our impartiality?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Cierto, aunque a veces la neutralidad solo sirve para respaldar el statu quo y no para prevenir el sufrimiento.
dialogue.translation: True, although sometimes neutrality only serves to support the status quo and not to prevent suffering.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Pero, ¿qué criterio usamos para decidir cuándo intervenir? Cada conflicto es distinto y surgen dudas sobre si la acción realmente ayudará.
dialogue.translation: But what criterion do we use to decide when to intervene? Each conflict is different, and doubts arise about whether the action will really help.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Podríamos usar el criterio de la 'responsabilidad de proteger', que justifica la intervención cuando el Estado no protege a su población.
dialogue.translation: We could use the criterion of the 'responsibility to protect', which justifies intervention when the state does not protect its population.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Eso suena bien en teoría, pero en la práctica la falta de voluntad política y de recursos suele ser un obstáculo enorme.
dialogue.translation: That sounds good in theory, but in practice the lack of political will and resources is often a huge obstacle.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Y aunque hubiera recursos, siempre hay consecuencias no deseadas: puede surgir un vacío de poder o un aumento de la violencia.
dialogue.translation: And even if there were resources, there are always unintended consequences: a power vacuum or an increase in violence may arise.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¿cómo justificar el costo humano? Quizás deberíamos preguntar a las personas afectadas si quieren nuestra intervención.
dialogue.translation: So, how can we justify the human cost? Perhaps we should ask the affected people if they want our intervention.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Esa es una buena idea, pero no siempre es posible consultar a la población; a veces hay que actuar rápido para prevenir una catástrofe.
dialogue.translation: That's a good idea, but it is not always possible to consult the population; sometimes we must act quickly to prevent a catastrophe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Me parece que en esta novela la herencia colonial se manifiesta sobre todo en la búsqueda de identidad del protagonista.
dialogue.translation: I think that in this novel the colonial heritage is manifested above all in the protagonist's search for identity.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero el autor no presenta una visión maniquea; el personaje es bastante ambivalente respecto a su pasado.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but the author does not present a Manichaean vision; the character is quite ambivalent regarding his past.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: También hay una clara crítica al colonialismo, aunque no se limita a denunciar, sino que propone descolonizar la mirada del lector.
dialogue.translation: There is also a clear critique of colonialism, although it is not limited to denouncing, but rather proposes to decolonize the reader's gaze.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exacto, y los personajes marginados, como el sirviente, no son meras víctimas; resisten de formas sutiles.
dialogue.translation: Exactly, and the marginalized characters, like the servant, are not mere victims; they resist in subtle ways.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: En ese sentido, el autor les da voz a los subalternos, algo que no siempre ocurre en la literatura canónica.
dialogue.translation: In that sense, the author gives voice to the subalterns, something that does not always happen in canonical literature.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Y no olvidemos el tema del exilio; el narrador escribe desde fuera, lo que le permite una perspectiva crítica.
dialogue.translation: And let's not forget the theme of exile; the narrator writes from outside, which allows him a critical perspective.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pero también hay una apropiación de la cultura del colonizador, una hibridación que enriquece la obra.
dialogue.translation: But there is also an appropriation of the colonizer's culture, a hybridization that enriches the work.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Totalmente, y el final sugiere una emancipación que no es solo política, sino también psicológica.
dialogue.translation: Totally, and the ending suggests an emancipation that is not only political, but also psychological.
